chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ibrahim b. Hashim, from Amr b. Uthman, from Muhammad b. Adhafir, from Abu Hamza, from Ali b. al-Hazawwar, from al-Qasim, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. He said:

Fatima (peace be upon her) came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) and mentioned to him the weakness of her condition. So he said to her: Do you not know what Ali's station is with me? He sufficed me in my affairs when he was twelve years old. He fought with the sword before me when he was sixteen years old. He slew the champions when he was nineteen years old. He relieved my sorrows when he was twenty years old. And he lifted the gate of Khaybar when he was twenty-two years old, even though fifty men could not lift it.

He said: Then the complexion of Fatima (peace be upon her) brightened, and her feet did not remain still until she came to Ali (peace be upon him) and informed him. So he said: How would it be if he had told you of all of Allah's grace upon me!

key_terms.الْأَبْطَال: the champions — warrior-heroes of the opposing forces at early battles
key_terms.بَاب خَيْبَر: the gate of Khaybar — a famous miracle at the Siege of Khaybar (7 AH)
key_terms.فَضْل اللَّه: Allah's grace/bounty — Ali's (as) acknowledgment that his virtues are divine gifts, not personal achievements
key_terms.مَنْزِلَة: station/rank — the Prophet's rhetorical opening highlights Ali's unparalleled proximity to him

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say to Fatima about Ali's rank and deeds from age 12 to 22?
ai.summary: The Prophet (s) comforts his daughter Fatima (as) by enumerating the extraordinary deeds of Imam Ali (as) at each stage of his youth, from age 12 to 22, culminating with the miraculous lifting of the gate of Khaybar which fifty men could not move. Historically, this hadith would have been told to Fatima (as) to reassure her of Ali's (as) divine standing and heroic stature during a period when she expressed difficulty. Ali's (as) humble response — that even greater divine favors remain unspoken — underscores the Shia theological concept of the Imam's boundless, divinely-bestowed excellence.
